about.bio:
Hi! I'm Pip - a product designer. I've been in tech since 2018.

At Ultraleap I led an interaction R&D team - proving the value of high fidelity hand tracking. I'm now at FitXR, designing fitness apps for people who hate fitness, across xr and mobile.

I combine simplicity and fun to create experiences that feel joyful and inevitable.

work.description: FitXR is a leading VR fitness app that transforms home workouts through immersive, gamified training.

experimentsIntro: Interaction experiments and prototypes - most made while leading interaction R&D at Ultraleap, some at FitXR, some just for fun.

experiments.title: Fidget Spinner
experiments.short: Count up and the shape morphs, bounces and spins faster
experiments.description:
A juice breakdown (a smoothie?) 🧃

🍎 Fluid shape morphing. The obvious one! Each shape had to feel as if it seamlessly flowed into the next - through its literal form, but also through the transition. Colour change, a scale bounce and extra rotation velocity help mask the SVG morph a little, so it feels like magic.

🍌 Bounces! Speaking of - bouncy transitions were a must. I focused on springy easing curves: watch the shape's scale bounce in and out, and the number overshoot.

🍊 Rotation velocity stacking. The shapes rotate smoothly, and each transition adds rotation speed (to make it feel extra exciting) before it falls off, so it never overstimulates.

🍇 Layout. A small one - I purposefully let bigger shapes overlap the number a little. It exaggerates the intensity of higher numbers and keeps things visually interesting. Full overlap would cause painful contrast issues.
experiments.imageAlt: A number counts from 1 to 7 and back; above it a coloured shape morphs from a droplet into ever spikier stars, bouncing and spinning faster with each step.

experiments.title: No Straight Line
experiments.short: Drag the words; ropes pull the rest along
experiments.description: An interactive poster: drag any word and the others follow, tugged along by springy ropes. A light Verlet rope sim, built with plain DOM and canvas.
experiments.imageAlt: Words on a blue poster being dragged around, pulling the others along on lime green ropes.

experiments.title: Workout Complete
experiments.short: A juicy workout-complete moment that didn't ship
experiments.description:
We decided not to ship this workout complete animation 😢 (we wanted to make sure we weren't slowing people down too much).

Pretty happy with the amount of juice in it - it will remain shipped in my heart 🧃🧃🧃
experiments.imageAlt: A workout's progress ring fills, the circle pops, and a burst of lime green ticks floods the screen before settling into one big tick.

experiments.title: Workout Nodes
experiments.short: A daily goal that unlocks, fills and lands with a tick
experiments.description: Playing with motion design at FitXR: the daily goal unlocks to show today's workout types, nudges you to come back tomorrow, fills its ring as you train, and lands on a satisfying tick.
experiments.imageAlt: A grey circle unlocks to show Dance, Flow and Box tags, a blue progress ring fills around it, and it turns into a lime green tick.

experiments.title: Fry Shower
experiments.short: Spin the dial, make it rain fries
experiments.description: A playful use of the circle slider: dial in how many fries you want, let go, and they shower down the screen.
experiments.imageAlt: Spinning the dial to choose how many fries, then letting go as fries rain down the screen.

experiments.title: Circle Slider
experiments.short: A dial that turns circular motion into input
experiments.description: A circle slider that turns circular motion into input. Uses velocity-based motion detection.
experiments.imageAlt: A circular dial being spun: a thumb travels round the track as the number in the middle counts up.

experiments.title: Murmurations
experiments.short: Paint a sunset, then flock starlings with the crank
experiments.description:
A Saturday experiment with a Playdate, p5 and flocking, trying to recreate starling murmurations at sunset 🌅

Create your sunset using the crank and d-pad, then play with your starlings: crank to change their direction, spawn more and pull them towards you 🐥
experiments.imageAlt: A flock of starlings swirling over a soft yellow and blue sunset in a browser, steered by a Playdate's crank shown in an inset.

experiments.title: Morandi

experiments.description: A concept + prototype for a daily art app, that generates prompts, inspiration, and critiques of your art.
experiments.imageAlt: The Morandi app: pick today's stick, get a drawing prompt with references, then log your art - it joins the row of sticks from previous days.
